name: What should I ask a builder before starting a rear addition?

mainEntity.name: Which questions help me compare contractors for a rear-house addition and avoid hidden costs or permit delays?
mainEntity.text: Which questions help me compare contractors for a rear-house addition and avoid hidden costs or permit delays?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rear addition is too complex to award based on price alone. Homeowners should ask whether the builder has completed similar projects in the same cities, how they handle permits and inspections, and who coordinates with the architect, engineer, and energy consultant. It is also important to ask how allowances are set, what is excluded from the bid, and how changes are priced if hidden conditions are discovered after demolition. Rear additions in Los Angeles often involve older framing, outdated systems, and tight site access, so the contractor’s problem-solving process matters a lot. A strong builder should be able to explain realistic timelines, how they protect the occupied home, and what could cause delays. The most useful contractor is not just the one with the lowest number, but the one who can deliver the project with fewer surprises and better coordination.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask about zoning experience, permit handling, structural coordination, schedule, allowances, contingency, and how change orders are priced. The best builder should explain how they handle plan checks, inspections, and the unknown conditions that often appear in older homes.
